channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen
item.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.

item.title: Was Vladimir Putin 'snubbed' by Xi Jinping? Viral handshake video is AI fake
item.description: A viral video appearing to show China's Xi Jinping "snubbing" Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit has racked up millions of views, fuelling speculation about tensions between Beijing and Moscow. But the footage is fake. FRANCE 24 traced the original video to an earlier summit, where the two leaders did shake hands. The creator, who runs a satire account, admitted to manipulating the footage using Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: 5 ways to turn off your 'work brain' after the day ends
item.description: Don't let your work troubles follow you home. Psychologist Guy Winch shares techniques to help you stop ruminating about your nine-to-five, so you can focus on what really matters. (Image credit: Beck Harlan for NPR)

item.title: Anthropic says it will put humanity first. Will its IPO change that?
item.description: Critics say now that the AI giant is a public company, its commitment to put safety ahead of commercial success will be tested. (Image credit: Michael M. Santiago)

item.title: The AI boom had a really bad week — and it's raising loud alarms
item.description: AI stocks — and the broader markets — got pummeled this week, raising major concerns about the financial system and the wider economy. Here's what to know. (Image credit: Spencer Platt)

item.title: An effort to circumvent the Electoral College may be within reach. But hurdles remain
item.description: A national effort to ensure that only winners of the popular vote become president could reach a critical milestone soon. (Image credit: Mark Felix)

item.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
item.description: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.

item.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.

item.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
item.description: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

item.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
item.description: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.

item.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
item.description: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

item.title: Live: France braces for fresh protests as social unrest enters sixth week
item.description: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

item.title: Nations at UN talks on AI killer robots agree to more talks but no firm commitment to rein them in
item.description: Efforts to establish rules for AI-powered killer robots and drones have run aground. U.N.-backed talks in Geneva ended Saturday with an agreement to extend discussions for two more years. (Image credit: Omer Urer)

item.title: German bidder stages last-gasp bid to rescue Poundland
item.description: A German investment firm has made a last-minute entry into the race to save Poundland, just days before its directors face the bleak prospect of appointing administrators to one of Britain's biggest high street retailers.

item.title: Ladbrokes-owner Entain in talks with CVC after gambling tax hit
item.description: The London-listed owner of Ladbrokes and Coral is in talks to sell part of its business to one of the world's biggest private equity firms as it tries to mitigate the impact of Labour's latest tax raid on the gambling industry.

item.title: US Agriculture Department and FBI hit by cyberattacks, media report
item.description: Hackers breached systerms at the US Agriculture Department and the FBI, US media reported, amid a recent wave of major technology disruptions across the country.

item.title: Denmark says it thwarted 'Russian plot' to kill US-Ukrainian rapper
item.description: Police thwarted a Russian plot to kill a US-Ukrainian rapper who was performing in Denmark, according to authorities.

item.title: Famed Marine Corps veteran under federal investigation over undisclosed allegations
item.description: The Naval Criminal Investigative Service says it is investigating a famed Marine Corps veteran over undisclosed allegations

item.title: England captain Harry Kane out injured for 'next few months'
item.description: England captain Harry Kane is expected to be out of action for a few months after tearing a ligament in his left ankle.

item.title: Man accused of starting blaze that became Palisades Fire found guilty of arson
item.description: The defendant was found guilty of two arson counts during a retrial.

item.title: WATCH: Tips for hosting Friendsgiving this year
item.description: Digital creator Kerra Masella shares her tips for planning and hosting a Friendsgiving celebration, from getting organized ahead of time to making friends feel welcome around the table.

item.title: NHS warns of 'alarming' rise in hospital admissions for 'silent killer'
item.description: NHS leaders are warning of an "alarming" rise in hospital admissions for high blood pressure across the UK.

item.title: Judge denies Alex Murdaugh's bid to dismiss murder charges
item.description: Murdaugh sought to throw out the case as he faces a retrial, after the South Carolina Supreme Court overturned his 2023 murder convictions.

item.title: WATCH: Is travel insurance worth it after the FAA ground stop?
item.description: Katy Nastro, travel correspondent at Flighty, shares what travelers can do to protect themselves.

item.title: House of Cards: America's enemies "no longer fear it, its allies no longer trust it'
item.description: The Economist's deputy editor Tom Standage joins us for a futuristic retrospective, taking us back to the future as we spotlight "The World Ahead 2027". We begin with the "leader of the free world", the FIFA Peace Prize recipient presiding over an America under the "Donroe Doctrine": "Its enemies no longer fear it and its allies no longer trust it in the way they did before."

item.title: S&P 500 sinks 3.7% and the Nasdaq composite goes negative for the year
item.description: AI stocks have hefty market values and have a much bigger impact on the market's direction. They were responsible for Wall Street's big gains this year and are now behind the big slide for the market. (Image credit: Seth Wenig)

item.title: Paris police officers sentenced to prison over 2020 beating of Black man
item.description: A Paris court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler, a rare such ruling. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.

item.title: Cold weather alert extended as temperatures drop to -10C
item.description: A cold weather warning has been extended as temperatures dropped to -10C (14F) overnight into Saturday.

item.title: Guinea bans Burkina Faso broadcaster, escalating diplomatic tensions
item.description: Tensions rise between Guinea and Burkina Faso after Conakry bans Burkinabe broadcaster RTB, amid a diplomatic dispute over gold miners and a caricature of President Mamadi Doumbouya. Meanwhile, fighting erupts between Congolese forces and the Rwanda-backed FRN group in eastern DR Congo, despite peace commitments. Finally, in Ethiopia, one entrepreneur is tackling period poverty by breaking menstrual stigma and making reusable sanitary pads more accessible.

item.title: MLK's handwritten draft of iconic speech on display for the first time
item.description: The only known handwritten draft of The Reverend Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech is on display in his hometown. The iconic phrase, however, never made it on the page. (Image credit: Lynsey Weatherspoon for NPR)

item.title: 'Licence to kill': France adopts law presuming 'legitimate' self-defence in police shootings
item.description: French senators gave final approval on Friday to controversial legislation granting police officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when using firearms, fulfilling a long-standing demand of the far right even as weeks of student-led protests have thrust the issue of police brutality back into the spotlight. Left-wing lawmakers have vowed to challenge the bill.

item.title: WATCH: New health warning on doomscrolling: What to know and tips to break the habit
item.description: A Lancet Psychiatry report calls problematic internet use a global health concern, affecting more than 1 in 10 people. ABC News’ Dr. Jennifer Miao explains the impact and how to protect yourself.

item.description: Welcome to the World This Week with Gavin Lee. You give us 45 minutes, we'll give you 7 days worth of crystal clear analysis. As ever, alongside a handpicked panel of four distinguished foreign correspondents.

item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.description: A sadistic predator has been sentenced to life in prison after being found guilty of the kidnap and first-degree murder of a vulnerable British woman.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis target Riyadh after Saudi coalition's 'special operation'
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launched strikes on Riyadh on Saturday after Saudi-led coalition air raids on Yemen, escalating a months-long surge in cross-border attacks.

item.title: Trump says he plans to penalize companies that build data centers in other countries
item.description: President Donald Trump says U.S. tech companies will face “a tremendous tax” if they build artificial intelligence data centers in other countries

item.title: 🦛 USA: Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s famous hippo, has died
item.description: 🦛Fiona, Cincinnati Zoo’s beloved hippo, has died aged just 9, after swallowing a knitted hat that fell into her enclosure. Born prematurely and weighing only 13kg, she captured millions of hearts around the world and became an internet sensation.

item.title: UK and EU strike ‘landmark’ deal to rebuild ties after Brexit
item.description: 🇬🇧🇪🇺 A fresh start after #Brexit? The #UK and #EU have agreed on a landmark #deal to rebuild ties, following a summit in Brussels this Friday. The agreement covers easier food export checks, youth mobility and carbon emission quotas.

item.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with singer-songwriters Mariam Doumbia and Zaho
item.description: Two women, two voices, two destinies: Malian performer Mariam continues her musical journey after the 2025 passing of Amadou, her partner in life and on stage. "Amadou and I sang about love. We wanted to share love with everyone. We sang of peace, of love, of justice."

item.title: ‘A more expensive EU is not a better EU’: Austria's Minister for Europe, Claudia Bauer
item.description: This week's programme hosted Claudia Bauer, Austria’s Federal Minister for Europe, Integration and Family while she was in Paris for the recent G7 meeting. She offered her thoughts on the diplomatic moves surrounding Ukraine, transatlantic relations, EU enlargement and a headscarf ban in Austrian schools that has caused disquiet. We also talked about the thorny negotiations involved in the EU’s next long-term budget: the Multiannual Financial Framework.

item.title: Trump hails 'fantastic' relationships with China's Xi, Russia's Putin after three-way talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump played up his "fantastic" relationships with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin during a White House press conference on Friday following his return to Washington after a first-ever trilateral meeting with the Chinese and Russian leaders. Here are key takeaways from his wide-ranging briefing.

item.title: Photography: A very French history
item.description: From its use as creative expression to documenting our everyday reality, photography has become an essential and widely-accessible medium since its invention. Did you know, however, that the technology was developed in France? FRANCE 24's Tanishk Saha takes a look at the French legacy of photography.

item.title: France investigates actor Depardieu, writer Houellebecq over alleged gang rape
item.description: French police are investigating allegations actor and convicted sex offender Gérard Depardieu raped and assaulted a woman with the complicity of bestselling author Michel Houellebecq during a 2018 film shoot, two sources following the case said Friday. The plaintiff has accused the film's director Guillaume Nicloux of being complicit in the abuse.

item.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' & 'Rivals': The big TV shows to watch this month
item.description: "Blade Runner" returns with a futuristic twist, while British bonkbuster "Rivals" is back with part two of season two. TV critic Dheepthika Laurent joins Eve Jackson to review the month’s big releases, including Netflix’s acclaimed Arctic comedy "North of North" and the lavish K-drama "Remarried Empress".

item.title: 'Danny Tommo' jailed for slashing migrant dinghy
item.description: Anti-migrant activist Danny Tommo has been sentenced to 15 months in prison after using a knife to slash a boat in the English Channel.

item.title: WATCH: Reporter goes undercover as porch pirate
item.description: A New York Times reporter went undercover as a porch pirate to help identify the best ways to keep your home and packages safe as package deliveries ramp up this holiday season.

item.description: Shares in Anthropic have fallen by more than 10% at Friday's open on Wall Street, just a day after their record-breaking Nasdaq debut, as part of a global stock market rout.

item.description: The excitement around the release of GTA VI is causing gamers to “call out sick” to play and has lit up Miami in Vice City colors. ABC News’ Ashan Singh dives into what the hype is all about.

item.description: Trump heads back to Washington after meeting with Xi and Putin -- the first sitdown between the three superpowers -- with no tangible diplomatic breakthroughs in hand.
